summary: The canvas 2D context draws shapes and text on a <canvas> element in the browser. You set a color with fillStyle or strokeStyle, then call a method such as fillRect() or arc().
notes: Each fill uses the most recent ctx.fillStyle, the same way Java uses the most recent g.setColor(...).
ctx.beginPath() starts a new shape. Without it, arc() adds to the old path and fill() can repaint shapes you drew earlier.
The canvas draws once and keeps the pixels. Nothing calls your code again unless you draw again yourself.
pitfall: Angles are radians, not degrees. ctx.arc(330, 60, 30, 0, 90) is meant to be a quarter circle but draws a full circle, because 90 radians is more than one full turn. A quarter circle ends at Math.PI / 2.
contrast: Canvas uses top-left (0, 0) with y going down like Java's Swing, not turtle's centered origin. Unlike Swing, canvas has no paintComponent: your script draws once when it runs, and you redraw yourself when something changes.
